name: Sonos Arc Ultra
summary: Sonos's flagship 9.1.4 Atmos bar, with a new Sound Motion woofer for deeper bass, Trueplay tuning and the best multiroom app around; add a Sub 4 and Era 300s for a full system.
verdict:
The Arc Ultra is the soundbar most people should measure others against. Sonos rates it as **9.1.4**, using **14 drivers** including up-firing and side-firing units and its new **Sound Motion** woofer, which squeezes noticeably more bass out of a slim cabinet than the original Arc. It decodes [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/), but not DTS:X.

**Size it to your TV.** A TV's width is about **0.87 × its diagonal**, so a 55-inch set is roughly 48 inches wide and a 65-inch about 57 inches. At around 46 inches wide, the Arc Ultra looks right under a 55-inch TV and fine under 65 or 75 inches.

**One HDMI port, so eARC matters.** The bar has a single HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) connection. Plug your sources into the TV, and make sure the TV's eARC port can pass lossless Dolby TrueHD Atmos; plain ARC only carries compressed Dolby Digital Plus. **Trueplay** room tuning includes a quick mode that uses the bar's own microphones, so Android owners can tune it too.

**The upgrade path.** Add a [Sonos Sub 4](/gear/sonos-sub-4/) and a pair of [Sonos Era 300](/gear/sonos-era-300/) speakers as rears and you have a genuine 7.1.4-style system with overhead rear effects, all wireless. That's a large total outlay, but you can buy it in stages.

Owners rate dialogue clarity and the app highly; the main complaint is the lack of DTS:X for 4K Blu-ray. See the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) roundup and [Sonos home theater review](/sonos-home-theater-review/).

skipIf: You watch lots of DTS:X Blu-rays or need HDMI inputs on the bar

name: Sonos Beam (Gen 2)
summary: A compact Sonos bar with virtual Atmos, eARC and the full Sonos app, ideal for smaller TVs and rooms, and easy to expand later.
verdict:
The Beam (Gen 2) packs **five drivers** into a bar about **26 inches wide**, with HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) and [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) decoding. It has **no up-firing drivers**; the height effect is created with processing, so think of it as a clearer, wider-sounding TV upgrade with a hint of height rather than a true overhead experience.

**Size check.** At about 26 inches it suits TVs from roughly 40 to 55 inches. A 43-inch TV is about 0.87 × 43 ≈ **37 inches** wide, so the Beam sits neatly inside its edges; under a 65-inch TV (57 inches wide) it looks undersized and struggles to fill the larger room those TVs usually go in.

**Room size.** Owners find it fills bedrooms and living rooms up to roughly 250 sq ft comfortably. Past that, it runs out of output before the [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/) does.

**Upgrade path.** Add a [Sonos Sub 4](/gear/sonos-sub-4/) (or the smaller Sub Mini) for bass and a pair of [Sonos Era 100](/gear/sonos-era-100/) speakers as rears and you have a real 5.1 system with excellent app control and Trueplay tuning. There's no Bluetooth, so music streams over Wi-Fi via AirPlay 2, Spotify Connect or the Sonos app.

It's the safest compact choice for Sonos households. See the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) roundup.

name: Sony Bravia Theater Bar 9
summary: Sony's flagship single bar uses 13 drivers and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping to create a wide, tall Atmos and DTS:X soundfield, with optional wireless subs and rears.
verdict:
The Bravia Theater Bar 9 is Sony's most capable single soundbar: **13 drivers**, including up-firing units, with Sony's **360 Spatial Sound Mapping** creating phantom speakers around and above you. Unlike the [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/), it decodes both [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/), plus IMAX Enhanced, which matters if you collect 4K Blu-rays.

**No HDMI input, so check your TV.** The bar has a single HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) port. All sources go into the TV, and the TV passes audio out. Here's the maths that matters: plain ARC only carries compressed Dolby Digital Plus (lossy Atmos), while eARC has the bandwidth for **lossless Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD MA**. If your TV only has ARC, a disc player's lossless track gets downgraded before it reaches the bar.

**Bar 9 vs Bar 8.** The [Bar 8](/gear/sony-bravia-theater-bar-8/) has **11 drivers** and a shorter cabinet. The two extra drivers and bigger body give the Bar 9 a wider, fuller presentation in larger rooms; in a small room the gap narrows.

**Expansion.** Sony's optional SA-SW3 or SA-SW5 wireless subs and rear speakers turn it into a full system. Streaming includes Wi-Fi, Chromecast, AirPlay and Spotify Connect.

Owners praise the spacious sound and dialogue clarity; the main complaints are the missing HDMI input and the cost of adding a sub. See the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) roundup and the [Sony home theater review](/sony-home-theater-review/).

name: Sony Bravia Theater Bar 8
summary: A shorter, cheaper version of Sony's Bar 9 with 11 drivers, Atmos and DTS:X, suited to mid-size rooms and 55–65-inch TVs.
verdict:
The Bravia Theater Bar 8 uses **11 drivers**, including up-firing units, and the same 360 Spatial Sound Mapping as the [Bar 9](/gear/sony-bravia-theater-bar-9/). It decodes [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/), [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/) and IMAX Enhanced, so it handles every common 4K disc format, which several rivals at this price, including the Sonos bars, can't.

**Match it to the room.** Bars with more drivers and wider cabinets throw a wider soundstage. The Bar 8's shorter cabinet is a better fit under 55- and 65-inch TVs (about 48 and 57 inches wide) and in rooms up to roughly 300 sq ft, where the Bar 9's extra width matters less. Owners report convincing height effects in rooms with flat, standard-height ceilings.

**Connections.** Like the Bar 9, it has a single HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) port and no HDMI inputs. Make sure your TV has eARC, not just ARC, or lossless Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD MA from a disc player won't reach the bar intact.

**Build it out.** On its own the bass is decent but limited. Adding Sony's SA-SW3 or SA-SW5 wireless sub is the biggest upgrade; wireless rears come next. Compare the total with a full system like the [Samsung HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/) before you commit.

Streaming covers Wi-Fi, Chromecast, AirPlay and Spotify Connect. See the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) roundup.

name: Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar
amazonQuery: Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar Dolby Atmos
summary: Bose's top bar adds A.I. Dialogue Mode and ADAPTiQ room tuning to up-firing Atmos drivers, with broad streaming support and an easy wireless expansion path.
verdict:
The Smart Ultra Soundbar uses **nine drivers**, including two up-firing dipole transducers, and decodes [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/). Its headline feature is **A.I. Dialogue Mode**, which separates voices from the rest of the mix and lifts them. For anyone who keeps riding the volume button to hear dialogue, that's the reason to buy.

**Room tuning.** **ADAPTiQ** uses a headset microphone to measure several listening positions and adjust the bar's EQ, a form of [room correction](/glossary/room-correction/). It's simpler than Dirac on the [Klipsch Flexus Core 300](/gear/klipsch-flexus-core-300/), but it noticeably tidies bass in boomy rooms.

**Build-out maths.** Bose's full system means adding the [Bose Bass Module 700](/gear/bose-bass-module-700/) and [Bose Surround Speakers 700](/gear/bose-surround-speakers-700/). Together those cost about as much as the bar itself, so the complete setup lands in the same price class as the [Samsung HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/), which includes sub, rears and four height channels in the box. If you know you want the full system, the Samsung is better value; if you want to buy in steps, Bose's modular path works.

**Connections.** HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/), optical, Wi-Fi with Chromecast, AirPlay 2 and Spotify Connect, plus Bluetooth and built-in Alexa. There's no DTS:X. Owners rate the dialogue clarity and app highly. More in the [Bose home theater review](/bose-home-theater-review/).

name: Bose Smart Soundbar
summary: A compact Bose Atmos bar with five drivers (two up-firing), TrueSpace upmixing, A.I. Dialogue Mode, Chromecast, AirPlay 2 and Alexa, plus a clever Personal Surround option using Bose earbuds.
verdict:
The Bose Smart Soundbar is a compact all-in-one for TVs in smaller rooms. It fits **five transducers** into its slim cabinet, **two of them firing upward** for [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) height, and uses Bose's **TrueSpace** processing to upmix stereo and 5.1 into a wider, taller presentation. **A.I. Dialogue Mode** balances voices against effects, which is the feature most buyers will notice first.

**Do the distance maths.** Sound level falls about **6 dB** every time you double your distance from a single source. Move from a 6 ft seat to a 12 ft seat and the bar needs four times the amplifier power to sound equally loud at your ears. That is why a small bar like this shines in bedrooms and compact living rooms, and why big, open rooms are better served by the [Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar](/gear/bose-smart-ultra-soundbar/) or a bar plus a [Bose Bass Module 700](/gear/bose-bass-module-700/).

**Streaming is a strength.** Bluetooth, **AirPlay 2**, **Spotify Connect** and **Chromecast built-in** cover every phone, and **Amazon Alexa** is built in; Bose Voice4Video can also control your TV and cable or satellite box by voice. Connect it to your TV's [eARC](/glossary/earc/) port so Atmos from TV apps passes through. A remote is included.

**Expansion is the upgrade path.** Add a Bose Bass Module and the [Bose Surround Speakers 700](/gear/bose-surround-speakers-700/), or pair Bose Ultra Open Earbuds as personal rear channels for late-night viewing. DTS:X is not listed. Compare it with the [Sonos Beam (Gen 2)](/gear/sonos-beam-gen-2/) in our [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) guide and with Bose's wider range in the [Bose home theater review](/bose-home-theater-review/).

name: JBL Bar 1000
summary: A 7.1.4 system with a 10-inch wireless sub and detachable battery-powered surrounds, plus three HDMI inputs, giving real rear sound without permanent speakers.
verdict:
The JBL Bar 1000 solves the rear-speaker problem cleverly: its two end caps **detach** and run on battery as rear surrounds, then clip back on to recharge. Add the **10-inch wireless subwoofer** and up-firing drivers and you get a **7.1.4** system that decodes [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/).

**Decode the numbers.** 7.1.4 means seven ear-level channels, one sub and four height channels: **12 channels** in all. JBL quotes **880 W** total system power; spread across 12 channels that's a marketing total, not a per-channel rating, but owners consistently report strong output in mid-size to large living rooms.

**HDMI advantage.** With **three HDMI inputs** (with 4K Dolby Vision pass-through) plus an HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) output, a disc player and streaming box can feed the bar directly. That sidesteps TVs whose eARC ports are flaky or which don't pass DTS:X, a common problem with single-port bars like the [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/).

**Battery reality.** The detachable rears need recharging, typically between long movie sessions. If you leave them out permanently, budget for remembering to dock them.

JBL's room calibration, Wi-Fi with Chromecast and AirPlay 2, and Bluetooth round it out. Its bigger sibling, the [JBL Bar 1300MK2](/gear/jbl-bar-1300mk2/), adds channels and output for larger rooms. See the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) roundup.

name: JBL Bar 1300MK2
summary: JBL's largest 11.1.4 bar system with detachable battery surrounds and a big wireless sub, built for large rooms and loud movie nights.
verdict:
The Bar 1300MK2 is the second-generation version of JBL's flagship. Like the [JBL Bar 1000](/gear/jbl-bar-1000/), its ends **detach** as battery-powered rear surrounds, and it ships with a **wireless subwoofer**. The difference is scale: **11.1.4** channels in a longer bar, aimed at larger rooms. It decodes [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/).

**Decode 11.1.4.** Eleven ear-level channels, one sub and four height channels: **16 channels** in total, versus 12 on the Bar 1000. More channels let JBL's beam-forming place effects more precisely across a wide room, which matters most when seats are spread across a sectional or two rows.

**Room size maths.** In a 300 sq ft room the Bar 1000 is usually enough. Above roughly 400 sq ft, or in open-plan spaces where sound leaks into the kitchen, the 1300MK2's extra drivers and bigger sub keep dynamics intact at the volumes movies need.

**Inputs.** Multiple HDMI inputs plus HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) mean you aren't reliant on the TV's audio passthrough, a real advantage over single-port bars. Wi-Fi streaming with Chromecast and AirPlay and Bluetooth are included.

The trade-offs are size and cost: the bar is long, and you're paying close to receiver-plus-speakers money. If you can run wire, compare it with a passive system like the [Klipsch R-625FA 5.1.2 system](/gear/klipsch-r-625fa-51-system/). See the [best Dolby Atmos home theater system](/best-dolby-atmos-home-theater-system/) roundup.

name: Samsung HW-Q800F
summary: A 5.1.2 Samsung bar with a wireless sub, up-firing drivers and SpaceFit room tuning; a strong mid-range choice, especially with a Samsung TV.
verdict:
The HW-Q800F is Samsung's mid-range Atmos system: a **5.1.2** bar with up-firing drivers plus a **wireless subwoofer**, decoding [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/).

**Decode 5.1.2 and the upgrade.** Five ear-level channels, a sub and two height channels. Add one of Samsung's optional wireless rear kits with up-firing drivers and it becomes a **7.1.4**-class system: two extra ear-level and two extra height channels behind you. Buy the bar now and the rears later, but check the combined cost against the [Samsung HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/), which includes everything.

**Room tuning and TV tricks.** **SpaceFit Sound Pro** uses a microphone to adapt the EQ to your room, a simple form of [room correction](/glossary/room-correction/). With a compatible Samsung TV, **Q-Symphony** lets the TV's speakers join the bar, and wireless Dolby Atmos removes the HDMI cable entirely.

**Connections.** HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) and optical, Wi-Fi with AirPlay 2 and Spotify Connect, plus Bluetooth. Owners report punchy bass from the included sub and good dialogue with Active Voice Amplifier; the bar is less convincing at overhead effects than larger systems with rear height drivers.

If you own a Samsung TV and want a complete-feeling system at a mid-range price, this is the obvious pick. See the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) roundup and [Samsung home theater review](/samsung-home-theater-review/).

name: VIZIO All-in-One Soundbar SE (SV210Y-08)
summary: A budget all-in-one Vizio bar with two full-range drivers and two integrated bass drivers, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X decoding, HDMI eARC and Bluetooth; there is no separate sub and the remote is sold separately.
verdict:
The VIZIO All-in-One Soundbar SE (SV210Y-08) replaces the V-Series 2.1 on our list as the cheapest worthwhile step up from TV speakers. It packs **two full-range drivers and two integrated bass drivers** into one bar, so there is no separate subwoofer to place, and Vizio rates it at **95 dB** of output. It decodes **Dolby Atmos and DTS:X**, connects over **HDMI eARC** so your TV remote controls volume, and doubles as a **Bluetooth speaker**. QuickFit thumbscrews attach it directly to select Vizio TVs.

**Put the 95 dB in context.** Movie reference level peaks at 105 dB per channel, so a 95 dB ceiling is 10 dB short, and 10 dB sounds roughly half as loud to most ears. In a bedroom or small living room, that is plenty for TV and casual movies; in a big open-plan space it runs out of headroom.

**Read 'Atmos' carefully.** With four forward-facing drivers and no up-firing or rear speakers, Atmos and DTS:X are rendered virtually; you will not get the overhead effects of a true 5.1.2 system. The difference is explained in [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/).

Two practical notes: the **remote is sold separately**, so plan on using your TV remote through [eARC](/glossary/earc/), and Vizio says to contact its support if your TV needs an optical connection. Advanced settings live in the Vizio mobile app, which requires a Vizio account.

If you can stretch, the [VIZIO 5.1.2 Elevate SE Soundbar (SL512X-08)](/gear/vizio-elevate-se-sl512x/) adds a wireless sub and rotating height speakers. More budget options are in the [best budget home theater system](/best-budget-home-theater-system/) guide.

name: Polk MagniFi Max AX SR
amazonQuery: Polk MagniFi Max AX SR soundbar
summary: A complete Polk Atmos system with bar, 10-inch wireless sub and wireless rear speakers, decoding Atmos and DTS:X with Polk's VoiceAdjust for clear dialogue.
verdict:
The MagniFi Max AX SR is the full-system version of Polk's flagship bar: the MagniFi Max AX bar with up-firing drivers, a **10-inch wireless subwoofer** and Polk's **wireless rear surround speakers** in one box. Polk rates the complete package as **7.1.4**, and it decodes [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/), [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/) and IMAX Enhanced.

**Decode 7.1.4.** Seven ear-level channels, one sub and four height channels. Rear speakers matter more than height in many rooms: they put effects genuinely behind you rather than relying on processing, which no single bar fully replicates.

**Value maths.** Compare the "bar + sub + rears in one box" price with buying each part separately. A [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/) plus a Sub 4 plus two Era 300s costs well over double. The Polk gives up Sonos's app polish and Trueplay, but includes every piece.

**Dialogue and connections.** Polk's **VoiceAdjust** raises the center channel independently, which helps with quiet dialogue. HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/), optical, Wi-Fi with Chromecast and AirPlay 2, and Bluetooth cover streaming.

Owners report strong bass from the 10-inch sub and convincing surround; the main complaints concern app reliability and occasional firmware quirks. If you want an all-in-one system with DTS:X and real rears for less than a Samsung flagship, it's a smart buy. See the [Polk Audio review](/polk-audio-review/) and [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/).

name: Hisense AX5120G 5.1.2 Soundbar
summary: A budget 5.1.2 Hisense bar with a wireless subwoofer, 420 W total, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, 4K HDMI pass-through and Bluetooth 5.3; the surround channels are built into the bar rather than separate rear speakers.
verdict:
The Hisense AX5120G takes the budget-Atmos slot on our list. It is a **5.1.2-channel** bar with a **wireless subwoofer**, rated at **420 W** total, and it decodes both **Dolby Atmos** and **DTS:X**. Connections are generous for the money: **HDMI eARC**, an **HDMI input with 4K pass-through**, optical, AUX, USB and **Bluetooth 5.3**. It is Roku TV Ready, so a Roku TV remote controls both, and seven EQ presets cover music, movies and news.

**Know where the surrounds are.** Hisense says the front, center and rear surround channels are all built into the bar. That keeps setup clean, with only the sub to place, but bar-mounted surround channels cannot put effects behind you the way physical rear speakers do. If true rear sound is the goal, choose a system with separate surrounds.

**Read the watts.** 420 W is a total across every driver and the sub, not a per-channel figure measured like a receiver's. Split across eight channels (5 + 1 + 2), it averages about **53 W**, and the sub takes a large share in practice. On paper that suits a small to mid-size living room rather than a large open-plan space.

Connect it to your TV's [eARC](/glossary/earc/) port for lossless Atmos from TV apps, or run a 4K source through its HDMI input. The formats are explained in [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/). For rotating height speakers in a similar price band, compare the [VIZIO 5.1.2 Elevate SE Soundbar (SL512X-08)](/gear/vizio-elevate-se-sl512x/); for real rear speakers on a budget, the [Sony HT-S40R 5.1 Home Theater System](/gear/sony-ht-s40r/) is an option. More picks in the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/) guide.
